model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the negative log probability of per-specialty medical terms for a base model (Mistralv0.2-Base, shown in light blue) and for versions of the model fine-tuned on six medical specialties: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics (each represented by a distinct shade of orange or brown). The horizontal axis lists the six specialties, and for each, there are seven bars: one for the base model and six for the models fine-tuned on each of the specialties (including the specialty itself). The vertical axis, labeled "Negative log probability," is scaled linearly from -27 to -22, with tick marks every 1 unit. Lower values on this axis (closer to -27) indicate higher probability, meaning better performance or higher likelihood of generating relevant terms. For each specialty group, the base model consistently shows the lowest negative log probability (highest probability), with values around -22.5 to -23.5. The fine-tuned models show varying performance: the model fine-tuned on the same specialty (e.g., Cardio fine-tuned on Cardio) typically performs best among the fine-tuned models for that group, with negative log probabilities ranging from approximately -24.5 to -26.5. For example, in the "Cardio" group, the base model has a negative log probability of about -22.5, while the Cardio-fine-tuned model has a value around -26.5, and the other fine-tuned models fall between these values. The bars are arranged in groups corresponding to each specialty on the x-axis, and within each group, the bars are ordered from left to right as: base model, then fine-tuned models in the order listed in the legend (Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, Pediatrics). The chart visually demonstrates that fine-tuning improves model performance (lowers negative log probability) on terms related to the specialty it was trained on, with the base model generally performing better overall across all specialties.
